1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nf6 5.N.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Panov Attack, Fianchetto Defence

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nf6 5.N.strategy: Takes the pawn before Black's fianchetto is ready. The pawn on d5 is attacked twice and defended once, so Black will win it back, and White should expect an open game with an isolated d4 pawn in return for active pieces.

A gambit of time: Black develops the bishop and prepares castling instead of recapturing at once. The d5 pawn stays attacked twice and defended once, so White must spend a move to hold it; if White manages, Black has given a pawn for little.
